subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC requirements
messages:
From: aditya.rao@redwood.inference
To: cara.taylor@finhealth.com, daniel.lee@finhealth.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-05T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC requirements

Cara / Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure I captured all of the requirements and next steps. Please correct me where I missed anything.

Pain points / drivers:
- Regulated workloads (PHI) require strict network isolation and customer-managed keys.
- Current vendor constraints: existing inference vendor doesn’t offer VPC-only deployment and billing visibility is a problem.
- Latency-sensitive use cases (real-time clinical suggestions) — need sub-150ms tail latency for 512-token prompts.

Current stack (what you shared):
- AWS account per environment (prod/stage), VPCs with EKS clusters, internal PKI, KMS for most secrets.
- On-prem archival for older records; data residency in us-east-1.

Success criteria for a Private/PVC deployment:
- Private control plane or dedicated private deployment inside FinHealth VPC (no public endpoints to inference workloads).
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration for key control.
- Network constraints: VPC peering or PrivateLink, support for strict egress rules, optional air-gapped on-prem bundle for future phases.
- SLA: predictable latency and throughput for production traffic, support for burst capacity during end-of-month runs.
- Auditability: logs (auth, admin, access) forwarded to your SIEM, and SOC2 evidence sharing for Redwood.

Open questions (items we asked you to confirm):
1) Which AWS account will host the Redwood instances (prod vs. shared infra)?
2) Can you share a redacted network diagram and firewall rules (egress / ingress) we should plan for?
3) Any mandatory third-party approvals for HSM/KMS integrations?
4) Expected go-live window (POC vs. production)?

Next steps
- I’ll send over our Private/VPC checklist and a proposed PoC plan (attached).
- If you can share the network diagram and SOC2 summary, our solutions team will review for architecture fit.
- Propose a follow-up technical deep-dive next week with your security/infra lead.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (Redwood checklist for Private deployments)

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0142

From: marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Date: 2026-10-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC requirements — proposed PoC plan and next steps

Cara / Daniel / Aditya —

Thanks for sharing the diagram and SOC2 summary. Quick response from the solutions side — see below for a proposed PoC and initial technical notes. Happy to go deeper on the call.

Proposed PoC scope (6 weeks):
- Week 0–1: environment prep — VPC peering / PrivateLink setup, KMS permissions and test key provisioning (redwood will provide cloudformation templates and a runbook).
- Week 2–3: deploy Private inference runtime in FinHealth prod account (dedicated instances), load sample dataset, basic integration testing (auth, telemetry).
- Week 4–5: performance tuning (batching configs, tokenization), latency SLO verification with synthetic traffic, quality checks on model outputs.
- Week 6: handoff and remediation, runbook delivery, and decision checkpoint for production rollout.

Technical notes / feasibility:
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS keys via cross-account grants. For HSM (BYOH) we have an integration path but will need compliance review and an HSM signing endpoint; we’ll document the exact flows.
- Network: PrivateLink preferred for minimal routing changes, but VPC peering is supported. We require a couple of outbound endpoints from the Redwood control plane to a narrow set of IPs (for management) — if that’s not acceptable we can discuss an offline control-plane model.
- Air-gap: We can provide an on-prem air-gap bundle for an isolated install. That path requires a longer lead time (2–3 months) and additional compliance review.
- Telemetry & Logs: We can forward structured logs to your SIEM over HTTPS or S3 ingestion; we’ll keep auth logs separate from application logs per your requirements.

Acceptance criteria for PoC:
- Successful key rotation test using your KMS; Redwood must not retain plaintext customer keys.
- Latency: 95th percentile < 150ms for 512-token requests under agreed synthetic profile.
- Auditability: auth and admin logs delivered to your SIEM for 30-day retention during PoC.
- Security review: preliminary checklist completed with no critical blockers.

Action items & owners:
- FinHealth: share full (non-redacted) network/firewall rules and SOC2 (legal NDA step) — Cara (owner).
- Redwood: provide CloudFormation templates and runbook for KMS grants + PrivateLink config — Marissa (owner).
- Scheduling: Aditya to coordinate 30–45m technical deep-dive with Daniel and Marissa.

Proposed slots (PT): Tuesday 10/13 10:00–10:45 or Wednesday 10/14 14:00–14:45. Let me know which works and I’ll reserve time.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-setup-brief.pdf (PoC runbook and checklist)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
